script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. CITY PARK - DAY

A beautiful SPRING day. A group of FRIENDS, all in their 30s, are picnicking.

JOHN (early 30s, serious, glasses) reads a book. JANE (mid 30s, quirky, red hair) paints. MARK (late 30s, joker) does a crossword puzzle. SARAH (early 30s, quiet, sensitive) listens to music on headphones.

MARK
(looking at crossword puzzle)
Hey, John, can I ask you a question?

JOHN
(looks up, a bit annoyed)
Sure, Mark. What's on your mind?

MARK
(grinning)
This word, 'forgiveness'. What does it mean exactly?

John looks thoughtful for a moment.

JOHN
Well, Mark, it means to let go of anger, resentment, and bitterness towards someone who has wronged you. It's about giving them a second chance, and moving on from the past.

MARK
(laughs)
Wow, that sounds like a tall order. Who would I even need to forgive?

Suddenly, RICH (mid 30s, brooding, scruffy) enters the scene, looking annoyed.

RICH
(angrily)
Hey, Mark. I see you're still wasting your time with these clowns.

Mark shrugs.

MARK
(smirking)
And here I thought you'd join us for a change.

Rich looks at the others, then at John.

RICH
(angrily)
You're the one who invited them, John. You're the one who keeps forgiving them for their bullshit.

John looks at Rich, then at his friends.

JOHN
(calmly)
Mark and the others have made mistakes, Rich. But they've apologized and tried to make amends. That's all I ask for.

Rich rolls his eyes.

RICH
(mocking)
Oh, the forgiveness tour continues.

Suddenly, SARAH puts down her headphones.

SARAH
(calmly)
Rich, we've all made mistakes. And we've all been forgiven. It's part of being human.

Rich looks surprised by Sarah's words, then at John.

RICH
(softening)
You know what, John? Maybe I should give them another chance.

John smiles.

JOHN
(encouragingly)
That's the spirit, Rich.

Mark smirks at Rich, then turns to John.

MARK
So, what about you, John? Who do you need to forgive?

John looks surprised.

JOHN
(shrugs)
Me? I don't think I have anyone to forgive.

Jane looks at John with a knowing smile.

JANE
(teasingly)
Oh really? Let me guess, you're perfect?

John laughs.

JOHN
(smiling)
Hardly, Jane. But maybe it's time I started looking for someone to forgive.

FADE OUT.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

John sits at a table, looking through an old photo album. He comes across a picture of himself and his SISTER, LUCY, as children. A waiter approaches.

WAITER
(clearing throat)
Another coffee, sir?

John looks up, then back at the photo.

JOHN
(to himself)
Yeah, I'll have another.

As the waiter leaves, John's thoughts turn to Lucy.

JOHN (V.O.)
(voiceover)
Lucy and I used to be close. But something happened when we were teenagers...

INT. HIGH SCHOOL - FLASHBACK

John and Lucy, both in their late teens, are arguing in the hallway.

LUCY
(yelling)
You always think you're better than me!

JOHN
(defensive)
I'm not trying to be better than you, Lucy! I just want what's best for myself!

Lucy storms off, leaving John standing there, confused and hurt.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

John's thoughts are interrupted by the sound of the door opening. He looks up to see Lucy entering. She looks older, but the resemblance is still there.

LUCY
(surprised)
John? Is that you?

John stands up, a mixture of emotions on his face.

JOHN
(stammering)
Lucy... I didn't think you'd come.

They stand there, unsure of what to say to each other.

LUCY
(hesitantly)
Can we... talk?

John nods, and they sit down at a table.

LUCY
(tearfully)
I've carried this anger and resentment towards you for so long. And I don't know why. I just... I wanted to apologize.

John looks at Lucy, then at the old photo album.

JOHN
(softly)
I've carried the same burden, Lucy. I'm glad we're here to talk about it.

They share a long, awkward silence, then Lucy speaks up.

LUCY
(smiling)
I've missed you, John.

John smiles back.

JOHN
(smiling)
I've missed you too, Lucy.

They share a hug, and the scene fades to black.

FADE IN:

EXT. CITY PARK - EVENING

The friends are packing up their things, getting ready to leave. Rich is looking at John with a new appreciation.

RICH
(grinning)
You know, John, maybe forgiveness isn't such a bad thing after all.

John smiles.

JOHN
(agreeing)
I couldn't agree more, Rich.

The sun sets over the park as the friends say their goodbyes, each of them with a newfound appreciation for the power of forgiveness.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
